purpose: Test the mechanism the producer flagged as an untested post-hoc note: that the r=5 excess of ~2^4 comes from four byte-conditions each holding at 2/256 rather than 1/256 (the AES DDT gives two value-pairs per differential).
measured_by: dispatching session (Bash) - coordinator-side corroboration, NOT independent validation
why: The producer explicitly recorded this as 'not tested; recorded so it can be attacked, not asserted'. A mechanism that predicts rather than describes is what decides whether the object can survive further rounds, so it is worth an hour.
method: Vary k = the number of genuinely active BYTES inside the single active plaintext word, k = 1..4, holding everything else fixed. If the excess is a product of k independent per-byte factors of 2, it should scale as 2^k. Two independent runs at different seeds and data sizes (N=2^30 seed 20260802, N=2^32 seed 777333111), combined.
finding: The excess RISES monotonically with the number of active bytes and SATURATES near 13-16x. That the excess is structured in the active-byte count at all is itself informative - it is not a flat property of the swap.
verdict_on_the_hypothesis: NOT CONFIRMED AND NOT REFUTED at this resolution. The discriminating point is k=1, where the k^2 law predicts 1 and the 2^k law predicts 2; the measurement is 1.60 +/- 0.57 and sits between them. Reporting this as a confirmation of either law would be reading a preference into Poisson noise - the exact failure mode this campaign has already committed once and withdrawn.
why_it_matters_for_depth: If the effect is a product of per-condition factors that saturate near 2^4, then each additional round multiplies in further conditions and the excess should fall rather than persist. That is consistent with the measured death at r=6 and predicts that raw data alone will not carry this object deeper - power has to come from a better statistic or from iteration, not from more trials. This is a prediction, stated so it can be checked, not a closure.
not_established: Which law governs. More resolution at k=1 and k=2 would separate them cheaply and was not run.
Any claim about AES security. No key recovery, no certificate, no efficiency claim.
Novelty, which is not assessed here in either direction.
